reason: This passage (1 Samuel 17) depicts the story of David and Goliath with multiple instances of Hebrew people actively expressing their views and perspectives. David questions the men about the reward (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶֽל־ הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים), Eliab criticizes David directly (וַיִּֽחַר־ אַף֩ אֱלִיאָ֨ב בְּדָוִ֜ד), Saul voices his concerns about David fighting Goliath, and Goliath himself speaks his challenge. Rather than discouraging expression, the text shows various characters speaking their minds and perspectives. What is evident is fear and hesitation in response to Goliath's intimidating military challenge (וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד - they were greatly afraid), but this is distinct from systematic discouragement of expressing views.
